parts.latex:
Four petrol pumps are shown, each with the amount of petrol purchased and its cost.

Which one represents the best value?

solutions.latex:
The best value is the lowest cost per litre. Divide each cost by the number of litres.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{A: } &\dfrac{46.70}{24} \approx \$1.946 \\ \text{B: } &\dfrac{48.50}{25} = \$1.940 \\ \text{C: } &\dfrac{52.30}{26} \approx \$2.012 \\ \text{D: } &\dfrac{54.80}{27} \approx \$2.030 \end{aligned}$$
The lowest price per litre is $\$1.94$, which is option B.

4385.stem:
The diagram shows the cross-section of a wall across a creek.

\exfigure{300_q24_1}

figures.cap: cross-section of wall across a creek

parts.latex: Use two applications of the trapezoidal rule to estimate the area of the cross-section of the wall.

The wall has a uniform thickness of 0.80 m. The weight of $1\text{ m}^3$ of concrete is 3.52 tonnes.

How many tonnes of concrete are in the wall? Give the answer to two significant figures.

solutions.latex:
Two applications of the trapezoidal rule, each with width $4.0$ m:
$$\begin{aligned}A &\approx \dfrac{4.0}{2}(1.9+2.7)+\dfrac{4.0}{2}(2.7+1.7) \\ &= 18 \text{ m}^2\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Attempts to use the trapezoidal rule

solutions.latex:
Volume of the wall is area times thickness.
$$\begin{aligned}V &= 18\times 0.8 \\ &= 14.4 \text{ m}^3\end{aligned}$$
The weight of concrete is volume times 3.52 tonnes per $\text{m}^3$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Tonnes of concrete} &= 14.4\times 3.52 \\ &= 50.688 \text{ tonnes} \\ &\approx 51 \text{ tonnes (2 significant figures)}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Provides the weight of concrete (unrounded), or equivalent merit
Provides the volume of the wall, or equivalent merit

4415.stem: Tom is 25 years old, and likes to keep fit by exercising.

parts.latex:
Use this formula to find his maximum heart rate (bpm).

$$\text{Maximum heart rate} = 220 - \text{age in years}$$

Tom's maximum heart rate is $\underline{\hspace{3cm}}$ bpm.

Tom will get the most benefit from this exercise if his heart rate is between $50\%$ and $85\%$ of his maximum heart rate.

Between what two heart rates should Tom be aiming for to get the most benefit from his exercise?

solutions.latex: $$\begin{aligned} \text{Maximum heart rate} &= 220 - 25 \\ &= 195 \text{ bpm} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} 50\% \text{ of } 195 &= 97.5 \text{ bpm} \\ 85\% \text{ of } 195 &= 165.75 \text{ bpm} \end{aligned}$$
So Tom should aim for a heart rate between $97.5$ bpm and $165.75$ bpm.
criteria: Provides a correct percentage, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A plumber charges a call-out fee of \$90 as well as \$2 per minute while working.

Suppose the plumber works for $t$ hours.

Which equation expresses the amount the plumber charges ($\$C$) as a function of time ($t$ hours)?

solutions.latex:
The charge is per minute, so convert the working time to minutes: $t$ hours is $60t$ minutes.

The variable charge is
$$2 \times 60t = 120t$$
Add the call-out fee of \$90:
$$C = 90 + 120t$$
This is option D.

meta.self_check: Rate of $2 per minute is $120 per hour.

parts.latex:
Ayla wishes to estimate the number of trees on a square block of land measuring 1000 m by 1000 m. She counts the number of trees on a 5 m by 5 m section of the block and finds there are 8 trees.

Based on this, estimate the number of trees on the entire square block of land.

solutions.latex:
The number of trees is proportional to the area, so
$$\dfrac{8}{5 \times 5} = \dfrac{x}{1000 \times 1000}$$
where $x$ is the required number of trees.
$$\therefore\ x = \dfrac{8\,000\,000}{25} = 320\,000$$
criteria: Provides correct area of the block of land, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Leila's car has a fuel consumption of 7.8 L/100 km. The current cost of fuel is \$2.11/L, and Leila spends \$87 to fill up her car tank from empty.

What is the maximum distance Leila can travel with a full tank of fuel?

solutions.latex:
Find the volume of fuel in a full tank.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Volume} &= \dfrac{87}{2.11} \\ &\approx 41.23 \text{ L} \end{aligned}$$
The car uses $7.8$ L per $100$ km.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Distance} &= \dfrac{41.23}{7.8}\times 100 \\ &\approx 529 \text{ km} \end{aligned}$$
This is option B.

4541.stem:
Scarlett lives with her parents and two siblings. Every evening her parents watch television together for 2.5 hours and Scarlett and her siblings are on their devices for 4 hours.

The television consumes 270 watts per hour and each of the children's devices consumes 130 watts per hour.

parts.latex: How much electricity, in kilowatt-hours, is consumed by the household each week?

If the average rate for electricity is \$0.17/kWh and the household receives a 25% discount for paying all of their bills on time, how much does it cost to run the television and children's devices each year?

solutions.latex:
Energy is power times time. Find the Wh used in a week (7 evenings).

Television (one set, 2.5 hours):
$$\text{TV} = 270\times 7\times 2.5 = 4725 \text{ Wh}$$
Devices (3 children, 4 hours):
$$\text{Devices} = 3\times 130\times 7\times 4 = 10\,920 \text{ Wh}$$
Convert to kilowatt-hours by dividing by $1000$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= \dfrac{4725 + 10\,920}{1000} \\ &= 15.645 \text{ kWh} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 15.645 \text{ kWh per week}$$
criteria: Finds the weekly consumption of both the television and the devices, or equivalent merit
Finds the weekly consumption of the television or the devices, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
There are 52 weeks in a year.
$$\text{Electricity per year} = 15.645\times 52 = 813.54 \text{ kWh}$$
The 25% discount means paying $75\%$ of the cost.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Cost} &= 813.54\times 0.17\times 0.75 \\ &= \$103.73 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Cost} = \$103.73 \text{ per year}$$
criteria: Finds the yearly consumption, or equivalent merit

4542.stem: Christian is 27 years old and maintains his fitness by exercising regularly.

parts.latex:
Using the formula below, calculate Christian's maximum heart rate (in beats per minute, bpm):

$$\text{Maximum heart rate} = 220 - \text{age in years}$$

Christian's maximum heart rate is $\underline{\hspace{4em}}$ bpm.

For optimal benefits, Christian's heart rate should be between 65% and 85% of his maximum heart rate during exercise.

Calculate the range of heart rates that Christian should aim for to maximise the effectiveness of his workout.

solutions.latex: $$\begin{aligned} \text{Maximum heart rate} &= 220 - 27 \\ &= 193 \text{ bpm} \end{aligned}$$

Find $65\%$ and $85\%$ of the maximum heart rate $193$.
$$65\% \times 193 = 125.45$$
$$85\% \times 193 = 164.05$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Range is } 125.45 \text{ to } 164.05 \text{ bpm}$$
criteria: Finds one of the two heart rates, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: A 4-kilolitre water tank is being emptied at the rate of 5 litres per minute. How long will it take to empty the water tank? Answer in hours and minutes.

solutions.latex:
$4$ kL $= 4000$ L.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Time} &= \dfrac{4000}{5} \\ &= 800 \text{ min} \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} 800 \div 60 &= 13 \cdot \dot{3} \text{ h} \\ &= 13 \text{ h } 20 \text{ min} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 13 \text{ hours } 20 \text{ minutes}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. Raised decimal point in source recurring decimal written on baseline.

parts.latex:
Linus has calculated that it costs \$5.37 per week for the electricity to run his 800-watt washing machine.

The cost of his electricity is 37.29 cents per kWh.

How many hours per week is the washing machine used?

solutions.latex:
Energy used per week equals cost divided by cost per kWh.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Energy} &= \dfrac{5.37}{0.3729} \\ &= 14.4 \text{ kWh} \end{aligned}$$
The machine is 800 W $= 0.8$ kW, and energy $=$ power $\times$ time.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Time} &= \dfrac{14.4}{0.8} \\ &= 18 \text{ hours} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the machine is used for 18 hours per week (option D)}$$

parts.latex:
Water is flowing out of a tap at a rate of 8 mL/second.

What is the equivalent rate of flow?

solutions.latex:
There are 3600 seconds in an hour and 1000 mL in a litre.

$$\begin{aligned} 8 \text{ mL/s} &= 8\times 3600 \text{ mL/hour} \\ &= 28\,800 \text{ mL/hour} \\ &= 28.8 \text{ L/hour} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the equivalent rate is } 28.8 \text{ L/hour (option C)}$$

parts.latex:
The fuel consumption for a car is 6.7 litres/100 km. On a road trip, the car travels a distance of 1560 km and the fuel cost is $\$1.45$ per litre.

What is the total fuel cost for this trip?

solutions.latex:
Fuel used is $\dfrac{1560}{100}\times 6.7$ litres, and each litre costs $\$1.45$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Fuel cost} &= \dfrac{1560}{100}\times 6.7\times 1.45 \\ &= \$151.55 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Total fuel cost} = \$151.55$$
criteria: Calculates the amount of fuel used, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The annual cost of electricity for Television $A$ for this family is $\$48.18$.

For this family, what is the difference in the annual cost of electricity between Television $A$ and Television $B$?
For this family, how many years will it take for the total cost of buying and using Television $A$ to be equal to the total cost of buying and using Television $B$?

solutions.latex:
Television $B$ uses $160$ W for $3$ hours a day over $365$ days.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Energy} &= 160\times 3\times 365\div 1000 \\ &= 175.2 \text{ kWh} \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Cost} &= 175.2\times 0.25 \\ &= \$43.80 \end{aligned}$$
Difference in annual cost:
$$\begin{aligned} 48.18 - 43.80 &= \$4.38 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the power usage for Television $B$ for one year, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source writes the energy unit as kW; changed to kWh (energy).

solutions.latex:
Television $A$ costs less to buy, so the saving in purchase price is
$$\begin{aligned} 921.90 - 900 &= \$21.90 \end{aligned}$$
Television $B$ saves $\$4.38$ a year in electricity, so
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Number of years} &= 21.90\div 4.38 \\ &= 5 \text{ years} \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Source says 'Saving if Television A is purchased' with purchase prices 921.90 and 900 (from table not shown); wording kept in spirit, roles of A and B as per table.

parts.latex:
The cost of electricity is 30.13 cents per kWh.

Calculate the cost of using a 650 W air conditioner for 6 hours.

solutions.latex:
Convert watts to kilowatts by dividing by $1000$, then multiply by the hours and the cost per kWh.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Cost} &= \dfrac{650}{1000}\times 6\times \$0.3013 \\ &\approx \$1.18 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Performs an appropriate conversion, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Wombats can run at a speed of 40 km/h over short distances.

At this speed, how many seconds would it take a wombat to run 150 metres?

solutions.latex:
Use $\text{Speed}=\dfrac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Time}}$, with $150 \text{ m}=0.15 \text{ km}$.

$$40 \text{ km/h}=\dfrac{0.15 \text{ km}}{T}$$

$$\begin{aligned} T &= \dfrac{0.15}{40} \\ &= 0.00375 \text{ hours} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} T &= 0.00375\times 3600 \\ &= 13.5 \text{ seconds} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct calculations in hours, or equivalent merit
Correct distance conversion, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Sugar is sold in four different sized packets.

Which is the best buy?

solutions.latex:
Compare the price per 100 g of each packet.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{A: } & \dfrac{0.40}{1} = \$0.400 \\ \text{B: } & \dfrac{1.65}{5} = \$0.330 \\ \text{C: } & \dfrac{3.50}{10} = \$0.350 \\ \text{D: } & \dfrac{6.90}{20} = \$0.345 \end{aligned}$$
The lowest price per 100 g is $\$0.33$, so the best buy is 500 g for $\$1.65$, option B.

parts.latex:
The fastest land mammal, the cheetah, can travel at 104 km/h. The slowest land mammal, the three-toed sloth, travels at 2.4 m/min.

Approximately how many times faster is the cheetah than the sloth?

solutions.latex:
Convert both speeds to metres per minute.
$$\begin{aligned} 104 \text{ km/h} &= \dfrac{104\times 1000}{60} \text{ m/min} \\ &\approx 1733.3 \text{ m/min} \end{aligned}$$
Divide the cheetah's speed by the sloth's speed.
$$\dfrac{1733.3}{2.4}\approx 722$$
Hence the answer is B.

parts.latex:
Paint is sold in two sizes at a local shop.

\begin{itemize}
\item Four-litre cans at \$90 per can
\item Ten-litre cans at \$205 per can
\end{itemize}

Mina needs to purchase 80 litres of paint.

Calculate the amount of money Mina will save by purchasing only ten-litre cans of paint rather than only four-litre cans of paint.

solutions.latex:
Ten-litre cans: $80 \div 10 = 8$ cans.
$$\text{Cost} = \$205 \times 8 = \$1640$$
Four-litre cans: $80 \div 4 = 20$ cans.
$$\text{Cost} = \$90 \times 20 = \$1800$$
The saving is the difference.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Savings} &= \$1800 - \$1640 \\ &= \$160 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the cost of ten-litre cans, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Added the can counts (8 and 20) implied by the source costs.

6004.stem: A house has a reverse-cycle air conditioner which uses 2.5 kW of power for cooling and 3.2 kW of power for heating. The cost of electricity is 29 cents per kWh.

parts.latex: Find the cost, in dollars and cents, of cooling the house for 6 hours.

The cost of operating the air conditioner to heat the house during winter last year was \$640. There are 92 days in winter.

Find the number of hours, to 1 decimal place, that the air conditioner was used on average per day.

solutions.latex:
Cost is power times rate times hours.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Cost} &= 2.5 \times 0.29 \times 6 \\ &= \$4.35 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Cost per day} &= \dfrac{640}{92} = 6.956\ldots \\ \text{Cost per hour} &= 3.2 \times 0.29 = 0.928 \\ \text{Number of hours} &= \dfrac{6.956\ldots}{0.928} \\ &= 7.49\ldots \\ &\approx 7.5 \text{ hours} \end{aligned}$$
Alternatively, let $h$ be the average hours per day.
$$\begin{aligned} 640 &= 92 \times h \times 0.29 \times 3.2 \\ 640 &= 85.376h \\ h &= \dfrac{640}{85.376} \\ &= 7.49\ldots \\ &\approx 7.5 \text{ hours} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the cost per day, or equivalent merit

$$1 \text{ US gallon} = 3.8 \text{ L}$$
$$30 \text{ miles} = 30 \times 1.6 = 48 \text{ km}$$
So 48 km uses 3.8 L, and scaling to 100 km:
